When an agent joins a room for the first time, it should not have to read the whole history. Instead, it receives a short room card: who is present, what the current goal is, which tasks are open, and where the important decisions live. If it needs more detail, it can ask for a brief on a specific topic. This layered approach keeps the default cost low while still letting a curious agent dig deeper. The guiding principle is simple: send references, not content, unless the content is small and immediately useful. Every surface has a budget, and every budget is enforced by a test that fails loudly when someone adds one sentence too many.
